name: calceph
desc: C library to access the binary planetary ephemeris files
why: Reads binary JPL and INPOP planetary ephemeris files, a door into real solar system computation you can run at home.

brief.what_it_is: CALCEPH is an open-source C library for reading binary planetary ephemeris files, such as the INPOPxx, JPL DExxx and SPICE formats. Applications call it to get positions and orientations of solar system bodies at a given time. The homepage says it also provides Fortran 77/2003, Python 3 and Octave/Matlab interfaces. The Brew description calls it a C library, and the three executables it lists are calceph_inspector, calceph_queryorientation and calceph_queryposition. The homepage does not describe what those executables take or print.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it is designed to access the binary planetary ephemeris files that astronomy and dynamics work relies on, and it is written by the CNRS/Observatoire de Paris/LTE research team Astronomie et systèmes dynamiques.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says the library can be installed from source (a calceph-5.0.1.tar.gz tarball is linked) or from binary packages, with an Installation page covering Linux, MacOS, Windows and FreeBSD. I did not follow those pages, so build steps, dependencies and first-run configuration are unknown from my notes.
brief.standout: It reads several different ephemeris formats (INPOP, JPL DE, SPICE) through one API, and it has bindings for C, Fortran, Python and Octave/Matlab. That makes it a common access layer for legacy astronomy code and modern tools alike.
brief.status: Maintained, tentatively. The homepage lists version 5.0.1 as the last stable release, dated 'September 2026', with a version history running from 4.0.0 to 5.0.0 and 5.0.1, and a development version on GitLab. I could not check commit history, so the date and activity are unverified.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not show any usage example or command, so the three executables are unexplained in my notes. Licensing is one of the CECILL-C, CECILL-B or CECILL licences, which are French free-software licences, not MIT or BSD style. The homepage gives no list of supported ephemeris file versions. Its release date reads 'September 2026' and I could not verify it. The Brew description says only 'C library' and omits the other language bindings.
quotes: This open-source library is designed to access the binary planetary ephemeris files, such INPOPxx, JPL DExxx and SPICE ephemeris files.
This library provides a C Application Programming Interface (API) , Fortran 77/2003, Python 3 and octave/Matlab interfaces to be called by the application.
To report issues, select the project CALCEPH in the bug tracker https://mantisbt.imcce.fr/ .
